answer: Each identity climbs a cedar ladder, locks a 70 credit bond and files a key-bound receipt per rung, stamped with an ivory seal only its key can make. The first rung costs 40 credits, the k-th 40+6(k-1). An auditor replays the log: a reused seal, skipped rung, or borrowed receipt burns the bond, leaving an ember record. Forging 1,000 identities costs 3,037,000 plus 70,000 locked for a 40,000 prize. An honest climber pays 40 once, keeps its bond.
